references.text: Job describes the warm south wind: "you who know when clothes become warm and the land lies still under the south wind" – this directly connects to Jesus' words that when the south wind blows, people say it will be hot ([ref:Job 37:17|Job 37:17]).

The preceding verse where Jesus mentions the cloud rising in the west and people saying rain is coming. Together with verse 55, this forms a pair of weather signs that people can interpret ([ref:Luk 12:54|Luke 12:54]).

Jesus' point with the weather examples: You who can interpret the appearance of earth and sky, but cannot interpret this time – hypocrites! Verse 55 about the south wind and heat is part of this rebuke ([ref:Luk 12:56|Luke 12:56]).

A parallel in Matthew where Jesus uses similar weather signs – a red sky at night means good weather, a red sky in the morning means stormy weather – to rebuke those who cannot interpret the signs of the times ([ref:Matt 16:2-3|Matthew 16:2-3]).

James describes how the sun rises with scorching heat and the grass withers – an image of the intense heat that Jesus refers to with the south wind, and a reminder that earthly signs have spiritual meaning ([ref:Jak 1:11|James 1:11]).
